title: Atmosphaera Incognita

description.main: An illustrated novella about the multi-year construction of a 20-kilometer tower reaching toward outer space.
description.extended:
Atmosphaera Incognita is a short novella about building a tower 20 kilometers high toward outer space, issued by Subterranean Press as an illustrated hardcover.

The story follows the multi-year construction of the tower, a modern take on the Tower of Babel legend, and concentrates on the perseverance, planning, and technology the project demands. It also describes the atmosphere itself, the layer between the planet and space, with its beauties and hazards. Patrick Arrasmith made the dust jacket and the interior illustrations. Subterranean lists the book at 104 pages, and Booklist describes the story as 93 pages.

According to Publishers Weekly, quoted on the publisher's page, Stephenson wrote the piece in 2013 for Hieroglyph, an idea-incubation project. It is a short work in a bibliography of long novels, set beside books such as Termination Shock at 720 pages.

notes: First edition, trade hardcover (Subterranean Press, 2019), illustrated by Patrick Arrasmith. The title is printed as Atmosphæra Incognita.

research_log.research_notes: Page count 104 from Subterranean and OpenLibrary; Booklist cited 93-page story. OpenLibrary dates it Jul 31, 2019; Subterranean gives 2019 only. Hieroglyph origin rests on Publishers Weekly as quoted by the publisher (single secondary source). Some listings spell the title 'Atmosphaera'; the ligature follows the jacket.
